claims.claim: The new rule reports a named function (function declaration or variable-assigned function) declared inside a React scope
claims.why: FunctionDeclaration and VariableDeclarator visitors call reportIfNestedJsxFunction, which requires isNestedInReactScope to be true.

claims.claim: A React scope is a function named like a component or hook, or one containing JSX
claims.why: isReactScope checks /^[A-Z]/ or /^use[A-Z]/ on the name, or containsJsx on the body.

claims.claim: The function is reported only when it returns JSX or null on every return path
claims.why: returnsOnlyJsxOrNull requires at least one return statement, and every return argument must satisfy isJsxOrNullExpression; concise arrow bodies must also satisfy it.

claims.claim: The function must be called directly by name to be reported
claims.why: isDirectlyInvoked checks whether any reference to the binding is the callee of a CallExpression.

claims.claim: Functions only passed as props are not reported
claims.why: If no reference is a call callee, isDirectlyInvoked returns false and nothing is reported.

claims.claim: Functions in non-React scopes are not reported
claims.why: isNestedInReactScope must be true; otherwise reportIfNestedJsxFunction returns early.
